analysis.title: NVIDIA Corporation: SEC Scrutiny Enhances Risk, but Valuation Provides a Cushion
key_insights: BofA maintains Buy and a $280 PO on NVDA (price $125.53) after media reports of an SEC investigation into its accounting practices. No details are available on the practices, transactions or periods under review.

The SEC probe compounds the delayed Form 10-Q and the CEO transition, adding uncertainty while investor confidence is already fragile. BofA says it is premature to draw conclusions on scope or financial impact.

Investors will likely scrutinize neocloud/emerging customers (~25-30% of sales, BofA est.) and direct/indirect China demand (~10-15%), together ~40-45% of revenue. BofA argues scrutiny is not the same as revenue impairment.
Stress test: if 25-50% of that ~40-45% revenue slowed, NVDA would still generate $10-11 pf-EPS vs BofA's $15 NTM, or ~13x PE vs ~30x historically. This is the basis of the valuation cushion.

LTM revenue mix: hyperscalers ~54% and AI cloud/enterprise/industrial ~39%, with neoclouds ~25-30% of total sales. Direct China Data Center revenue is under 2% last quarter and effectively zero in forecasts.

Indirect China exposure arises through cloud infrastructure legally operated outside the US. Of ~30% of revenue shipped overseas, perhaps half could be accessed by China-based users, giving ~15% combined direct/indirect exposure. INTC, AMD, AVGO and QCOM face similar exposure.
The key question is whether revenue recognition, customer economics, financing arrangements and end-user exposure withstand heightened regulatory scrutiny.

As of FQ3'27 NVDA disclosed ~$32bn of neocloud agreements across FY28-32 (<1% of cumulative revenue, BofA est.), plus ~$3.5bn of land/power/shell guarantees. Commitments become operative only when counterparties secure financing and compute is deployed.

NVDA disclosed ~$105bn of credit support tied to land and power development in Ohio (SB Energy), available across customers. BofA says counterparty risk and the link between financing and demand warrant examination, but headline commitments are not financed revenue or losses.
Exhibit 1 totals ~$407bn of NVDA ecosystem commitments (~$85bn equity, ~$27bn license/hire, ~$170bn signed backstops, ~$295bn including MOU) vs ~$500bn CY26-27E FCF.
Exhibit 2 shows $518bn of future commitments (mostly $390bn supply and capacity, $203bn in FY28), $32bn additional neocloud commitments and $118bn guarantees.

BofA expects volatility to stay elevated until clarity on the SEC inquiry, the 10-Q and CY27 cloud capex plans, likely from early next year. The PO uses 16x CY27E PE ex cash vs a 15x-56x historical forward PE range.

market_movers.rationale: BofA keeps Buy on the valuation cushion even if 25-50% of neocloud and China-exposed revenue slows. Stock is at $125.53, near the 52-week low of $124.50.

sector_views.rationale: BofA remains constructive on NVDA given its leading share in AI compute and networking, and sees regulatory scrutiny as not equal to revenue loss.

earnings_insights: NVDA Form 10-Q for FQ3'27 is delayed, with no filing date given in the report.
BofA estimates NTM pro forma EPS of $15, forecast. A stress case of 25-50% slowing in neocloud and China revenue gives $10-11 pf-EPS, BofA scenario estimate.
PO basis is 16x CY27E PE ex cash, BofA estimate.

trade_ideas.description: Long NVDA stock, Buy with $280 PO
trade_ideas.rationale: Valuation cushion: even with 25-50% of exposed revenue slowing, EPS of $10-11 implies ~13x PE vs ~30x historically.
trade_ideas.risk: SEC probe scope, delayed 10-Q, CEO transition, China restrictions, neocloud counterparty risk.

risk_factors: SEC probe of accounting practices could produce unexpected scrutiny or impact to reported sales and financial statements.
Leadership transition and reputational risk from US government scrutiny around the NVDA CEO.
Larger than expected impact from China compute shipment restrictions.
Neocloud counterparty risk and the financing-to-demand linkage, including GPU-backed financing and backstops.
Competition from public firms, internal cloud projects and private AI companies.
Lumpy sales in enterprise, data center and autos, possible deceleration of capital returns, and antitrust scrutiny of NVDA's dominant AI chip position.
vol_and_positioning: BofA expects NVDA volatility to stay elevated until there is clarity on the SEC inquiry, the 10-Q, and CY27 cloud capex plans, likely from early next year.
NVDA trades at ~13x PE on the stressed $10-11 EPS vs ~30x historically, and the stock sits near its 52-week low of $124.50 (range $124.50-$243.37).
geopolitical: Direct and indirect China demand for NVDA compute is subject to BIS export-control rules. China retains access via cloud infrastructure operated outside the US.
US government scrutiny around the NVDA CEO and potential additional restrictions on compute shipments to China are cited as risks.

tension_points.bull_case: Even if 25-50% of neocloud and China revenue slowed, NVDA would earn $10-11 pf-EPS, about 13x PE vs ~30x historically.
tension_points.bear_case: The SEC probe, delayed 10-Q and CEO transition compound uncertainty. Neocloud financing, backstops and guarantees raise counterparty and revenue recognition questions.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Clarification from the SEC inquiry or the 10-Q showing material revenue recognition or financing issues, or weaker CY27 cloud capex plans, likely from early next year.

theme_stances.key_argument: Scrutiny is not equivalent to revenue impairment, and valuation provides a cushion even under stressed EPS.
theme_stances.evidence: scrutiny is not equivalent to revenue impairment

theme_stances.key_argument: Structures warrant examination, but headline commitments should not be treated as financed revenue or losses to NVDA.
theme_stances.evidence: headline commitment values should not automatically be treated as financed revenue or losses
